verdicts.argument: The contractor’s claim of a duplicate position is not substantiated by any contractual text that explicitly merges or overlaps the two positions.
No contractual provision indicates that positions 2.1.4.90 and 2.1.1.50 are intended to be combined or that one supersedes the other.
The contract does not contain any clause that merges 2.1.4.80 with 2.1.1.40, so the positions remain distinct.
There is no textual basis in the contract for treating 2.1.4.100 and 2.1.1.60 as a single position.
The contract does not provide a provision that merges 2.1.4.60 with 2.1.1.20; they are separate items.
The contract does not contain a requirement for additional scope or duration details beyond what is stated in the position texts.
The contract does not contain a clause that disallows foreign currency payment; the payment term is stated as USD but no unfairness is proven.
No contractual text merges 2.1.4.70 with 2.1.1.30; they remain separate positions.
The contract does not specify concrete class or reinforcement details for the shaft; the omission is not explicitly prohibited by the provided texts.
The contract does not contain a calculation formula that would invalidate the stated GP; the discrepancy is not proven by the texts.
The contract does not reference the outdated DIN 18195 as a valid standard; the use of the old norm is not explicitly prohibited by the provided texts.
The contract does not contain a clause that mandates the use of DIN 18531–18535; the reference to DIN 18195 is not explicitly disallowed by the provided texts.
